paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of samples across categories of ambiguity standard deviation and maximum ambiguity. The chart contains six slices, displayed as two concentric rings; an outer ring representing ambiguity standard deviation, and an inner ring representing maximum ambiguity. The outer ring includes slices labeled “Std: 0.0” (dark blue, 49.0%), “Std: 0.47” (light blue, 38.0%), “Std: 0.82” (blue, 7.0%), and “Std: 0.94” (cyan, 5.0%). The inner ring shows “Max: 1” (light teal, 39.0%), “Max: 2” (teal, 47.7%), and “Max: 3” (pale teal, 14.2%). A legend is included to identify the labels and corresponding colors for each slice. Percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The slices appear to be ordered in a descending fashion based on the size of their corresponding segments, both within and between the rings.
